title: Metals and Non-metals - Kid-friendly science workshop with tiny lessons and quick quizzes

questions.question: What does metallic lustre mean?
questions.explanation: Lustre means shine.

questions.question: Which property allows a metal to be hammered into sheets?
questions.explanation: Malleability is the ability to form sheets.

questions.question: Which property allows a metal to be drawn into wires?
questions.explanation: Ductility is needed for making wires.

questions.question: Why is copper widely used in electrical wiring?
questions.explanation: Copper is an excellent conductor.

questions.question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the common liquid metal.

questions.question: Which metal is soft enough to cut with a knife?
questions.explanation: Sodium is unusually soft for a metal.

questions.question: What does sonorous mean?
options: Makes a ringing sound when struck
questions.explanation: Metals such as bells are described as sonorous.

questions.question: Which non-metal is a well-known conductor exception?
questions.explanation: Graphite conducts electricity even though it is a non-metal.

modules.name: M1: Reactions of Metals and Non-metals

questions.question: When a metal reacts with oxygen, what is commonly formed?
questions.explanation: Metal + oxygen usually forms a metal oxide.

questions.question: What gas is often produced when a metal reacts with an acid?
questions.explanation: Metal-acid reactions commonly release hydrogen.

questions.question: Which pair of metals is stored carefully because it reacts very strongly?
questions.explanation: Sodium and potassium are highly reactive.

questions.question: Many metal oxides are
questions.explanation: Metal oxides often show basic character.

questions.question: Many non-metal oxides are
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides commonly show acidic character.

questions.question: An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases is called
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are common amphoteric examples.

questions.question: Why do metals show different speeds of reaction?
options: Because they all have the same reactivity
questions.explanation: Reactivity differences explain reaction speed.

questions.question: Which metal reaction clue may show that hydrogen is being produced?
questions.explanation: Gas release is often seen as fizzing.

questions.question: What can a more reactive metal do to a less reactive metal in a compound?
questions.explanation: Displacement depends on reactivity order.

questions.question: Highly reactive metals are usually found in nature as
questions.explanation: Highly reactive metals usually combine with other substances.

questions.question: Less reactive metals may sometimes be found
questions.explanation: Gold and similar metals can occur free in nature.

questions.question: What type of compound often forms when metals react with non-metals?
questions.explanation: Metal-non-metal reactions often produce ionic compounds.

questions.question: Ionic compounds usually have
options: very low melting points like ice cream
questions.explanation: Strong ionic attraction gives high melting points.

questions.question: When do ionic compounds conduct electricity well?
options: When molten or dissolved in water
questions.explanation: Ions need freedom to move in order to conduct.

questions.question: Why do solid ionic compounds conduct poorly?
options: They have no charges at all
questions.explanation: In the solid state the ions are fixed in place.

questions.question: Which idea helps explain both metal extraction and displacement reactions?
questions.explanation: Reactivity is the connecting idea.

questions.question: What is rusting?
questions.explanation: Rusting is the corrosion of iron.

questions.question: Which two things are important for rusting iron?
questions.explanation: Rusting needs both oxygen and moisture.

questions.question: Which method can help protect iron from rusting?
questions.explanation: Protective coatings reduce contact with air and water.

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: A mixture made to improve metal properties
questions.explanation: Alloys are designed mixtures.

questions.question: Why is pure gold often mixed with other metals?
options: To turn it into a gas
questions.explanation: Pure gold is soft, so jewellery uses harder mixtures.

questions.question: Which material is an alloy widely used for strength?
questions.explanation: Steel is a useful strong alloy.

questions.question: Why do engineers use alloys?
options: To get better properties than pure metals
questions.explanation: Alloys can be stronger or more corrosion-resistant.

questions.question: Corrosion is a problem because it
questions.explanation: Corrosion weakens and damages metal structures.
